when.python: a pyproject.toml, setup.py or *.py at the top level
when.settings: the code reads environment variables (os.environ / getenv)
when.publishes: the project is published as a package or image (pyproject [project] name, or a Dockerfile)
when.deps: the project has dependencies or adapted third-party code

items.fix: Write it in this order: tagline, why, 3-step install, what it does, security, limits, roadmap, FAQ, licence (template/README.md).
Paste the licence's official text unedited; your name goes in NOTICE or the copyright line the licence asks for.
Start with secrets (.env, .env.*, keys), then build output and caches (template/.gitignore).
Say how to report privately (GitHub advisories) and a response time you can keep (template/SECURITY.md).
Set-up, how to run the tests and checks, pull request rules (template/CONTRIBUTING.md).
Contributor Covenant 2.1 with a project contact address, never a personal email.
Keep a Changelog format with an Unreleased section on top.
Set indent, charset and final newline for every editor.
Add `* text=auto` so line endings stay consistent.
A beginner path: every step, with what the user should see after it.
Run the tests on every supported version, plus link and generated-section checks; actions pinned by commit SHA.
Update dependencies, GitHub Actions and (with Docker) images.
A bug form asking for version, steps and output, with a 'remove secrets first' note.
Turn off blank issues; link private security reporting and Discussions.
A short checklist: tests, changelog, docs.
Enable code scanning on pushes and pull requests.
Name who reviews each part, so branch rules can require them.
Name, version, licence, authors, URLs, entry point and a test extra (template/pyproject.toml).
Copyright line plus credits for adapted code (Apache projects).
List dependencies and adapted code: source, copyright, licence and what changed.
Every setting the code reads, with a comment and no real values.
Every setting: default, what it does, an example; stable headings other files can link to.
Exclude .env, .env.* and *.bak (keep !.env.example) before anything else: COPY . . copies secrets too.
On a version tag: test, build, trusted publishing with a required reviewer, a GitHub release with SHA256SUMS.
One-time setup and a per-release checklist.
